parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe and explain the variation in the solubilities of the hydroxides of the Group 2 elements.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The table lists the standard enthalpy changes of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}$, for some compounds and aqueous ions.

| species | $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}/\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Ba}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ | $-538$ |
| $\text{OH}^{-}\text{(aq)}$ | $-230$ |
| $\text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)}$ | $-394$ |
| $\text{BaCO}_{3}\text{(s)}$ | $-1216$ |
| $\text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)}$ | $-286$ |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Reaction 1 occurs when $\text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)}$ is bubbled through an aqueous solution of $\text{Ba(OH)}_{2}$.

Use the data in the table to calculate the standard enthalpy change for reaction 1, $\Delta H_{\text{r}1}^{\ominus}$.

$$\text{Ba(OH)}_{2}\text{(aq)} + \text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{BaCO}_{3}\text{(s)} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)} \quad \text{reaction 1}$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
If $\text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)}$ is bubbled through an aqueous solution of $\text{Ba(OH)}_{2}$ for a long time, the precipitated $\text{BaCO}_{3}\text{(s)}$ dissolves, as shown in reaction 2.

$$\text{BaCO}_{3}\text{(s)} + \text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Ba(HCO}_{3})_{2}\text{(aq)} \quad \text{reaction 2}$$

The standard enthalpy change for reaction 2, $\Delta H_{\text{r}2}^{\ominus}, = -26\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Use this information and the data in the table to calculate the standard enthalpy change of formation of the $\text{HCO}_{3}^{-}\text{(aq)}$ ion.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
(b)(iv)
parts.text:
How would the value of $\Delta H_{\text{r}3}^{\ominus}$ compare with the value of $\Delta H_{\text{r}4}^{\ominus}$ for the similar reaction with $\text{Ca(OH)}_{2}\text{(aq)}$ as shown in reaction 4? Explain your answer.

$$\text{Ca(OH)}_{2}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{CO}_{2}\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{Ca(HCO}_{3})_{2}\text{(aq)} \quad \text{reaction 4}$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The standard entropy change for reaction 1 is $\Delta S_{\text{r}1}^{\ominus}$.

Suggest, with a reason, how the standard entropy change for reaction 3 might compare with $\Delta S_{\text{r}1}^{\ominus}$.
